active.reliability: The 2.0L engine and conventional automatic are generally durable and comparatively simple. At 118k miles, require timing-belt records and inspect rust, suspension, cooling-system condition and transmission shifts.
active.safety: IIHS rated the original moderate-front and head-restraint tests Good. Side performance improved to Good only for cars built after November 2009; confirm the driver-door build date and stability-control equipment before treating this one as the stronger version.
active.verdict: The best balance of mileage, simplicity and price in today’s private-party set
active.note: The listing shows a clean title, 117,884 miles and no disclosed mechanical issue, making this the clearest Facebook candidate. The trim, VIN, build date and service history are not shown, so those items plus an independent inspection are mandatory before purchase.

active.reliability: The 2.0L engine and conventional automatic are generally durable, and the seller reports one-owner care with regular servicing at a Mazda dealer. At 201k miles, inspect for oil or cooling leaks, carbon buildup, worn mounts and suspension, transmission shift quality and Northeast rust, and verify every service record.
active.safety: IIHS named the 2012 Mazda3 hatchback a Top Safety Pick after Good original moderate-front, side, roof-strength and head-restraint results. Stability control and side-curtain airbags were standard; verify all warning lights, tires and recall completion using the actual VIN.
active.verdict: Strong crash protection and a good drivetrain, with unusually high mileage as the deciding risk
active.note: The current individual listing shows a clean title, one-owner history, regular Mazda-dealer servicing and no significant disclosed problem. Those claims and the VIN still need documentary verification; obtain title and recall checks, an insurance quote for a 16-year-old and a thorough independent inspection before payment.

active.tag: New today · strongest new safety/value case
active.reliability: The naturally aspirated 2.0L engine and conventional automatic are simpler than Volkswagen turbo or DSG combinations, and the seller reports four newer tires. At 138k miles, demand timing-belt and fluid-service records and inspect for oil or coolant leaks, cooling-system and electrical faults, rough shifts, suspension wear and Northeast rust.
active.safety: IIHS rated the 2014 Jetta Good in the original moderate-front, side, roof-strength and head-restraint tests, with a Marginal driver-side small-overlap result for cars built after October 2012. Stability control and side-curtain airbags were standard on the sedan; verify the build date, warning lights, tires, brakes and recall completion.
active.verdict: A useful newer-sedan safety case at a fair price, provided the missing service history checks out
active.note: The live individual listing shows a clean paid-off title, two owners, 138,000 miles and four newer tires, but gives little maintenance detail and does not show the VIN. Confirm seller ownership and lien status, obtain timing-belt and transmission records, run title and recall checks, price insurance for a 16-year-old, and require an independent inspection before payment.

active.reliability: The 1.8L Nu MPI engine and conventional automatic are comparatively simple, and the seller reports regular service, 2025 brakes and rotors, recent tires and alignment, and a completed ignition recall. This engine family can develop oil consumption or bearing noise, so check oil level and service records, listen for knock from a cold start, and inspect the cooling system, mounts, transmission and Northeast rust.
active.safety: IIHS results applying to 2015–16 Forte sedans were Good in the original moderate-front, side, roof-strength and head-restraint tests, but Marginal in the driver-side small-overlap test. Curtain and torso airbags were standard; this car predates modern crash-prevention equipment, so verify warning lights, tires, brakes and recall completion by VIN.
active.verdict: The clearest new Facebook prospect, with useful ownership and maintenance detail but meaningful engine-risk questions
active.note: The seller states two owners, ownership since 2017, a clean paid-off title, recent brakes and tires, and a completed ignition recall, while disclosing minor cosmetic damage. Verify those records and the VIN, run title and recall checks, price insurance for a 16-year-old, and require an independent inspection with special attention to oil use, engine noise and rust before payment.

active.reliability: The 1.8L engine and 5-speed manual are generally durable and avoid automatic-transmission risk, but 195k miles creates broad wear exposure. The seller reports a recent slave cylinder and oil service while disclosing one accident and a small exhaust leak; inspect the clutch hydraulics, exhaust, cooling system, mounts, suspension, rust and repaired structure.
active.safety: IIHS rated the 2006–11 Civic coupe Good in the original moderate-front test, Acceptable in the side test and Good for head restraints. Curtain and torso airbags were standard, but electronic stability control on this EX was not verified; the two-door body and unverified accident repair are added cautions for a new driver.
active.verdict: Good basic crashworthiness at a low price, offset by mileage, accident history and repair needs
active.note: The current listing shows a clean title, smooth shifting, new clutch slave cylinder, recent oil service and a disclosed small exhaust leak, plus one accident. Verify the VIN, title, repair records and stability-control equipment, get an insurance quote for a 16-year-old, and require a structural and mechanical inspection before payment.

active.reliability: The 2.5L engine avoids the older timing-belt design, but early fourth-generation Foresters can develop oil-consumption, CVT valve-body or bearing problems, and 182k miles magnifies that repair exposure. The seller reports recent front and right-rear wheel bearings and an August oil change; verify oil use, CVT service and behavior, cooling, suspension, wheel bearings and underbody rust.
active.safety: IIHS rated the 2014 Forester Good in the driver small-overlap, original moderate-front, side, roof-strength and head-restraint tests. It met Top Safety Pick criteria; the higher Top Safety Pick+ award required optional EyeSight front-crash prevention, which this listing does not verify, so do not assume it is equipped.
active.verdict: Excellent basic crashworthiness and useful size, balanced against serious high-mileage oil and CVT risk
active.note: The live private-party listing states a clean title, no major problem, recent wheel bearings and oil service, while disclosing cosmetic flaws and tires due soon. Verify the VIN, ownership, title and service records, budget four tires, check recalls and insurance cost, and require a Subaru-experienced independent inspection before payment.

active.reliability: The conventional automatic is durable and the seller reports ownership since 2016 plus recent battery, rear brake, rotor, stabilizer-bushing and oil work. The 2.4L 2AZ-FE is known for oil consumption and this example has nearly 237k miles, so verify the oil-use history and inspect the head-bolt threads, cooling system, transmission, suspension and rust closely.
active.safety: IIHS rated the 2009 Camry Good in the original moderate-front, side, roof-strength and head-restraint tests. Side-curtain airbags were standard, but electronic stability control was optional on four-cylinder LE cars; confirm this exact car has functioning stability control, ABS and no warning lights, then verify recall completion by VIN.
active.verdict: A transparent, inexpensive nearby fallback whose very high mileage prevents a higher rank
active.note: The seller provides the VIN, states a clean paid-off title and long ownership, and lists several recent repairs, which is better disclosure than most sub-$5,000 listings. Nearly 237,000 miles creates substantial failure risk, so confirm every record, run title and recall checks, get an insurance quote and require a compression, cooling-system, underbody and oil-consumption inspection before payment.

active.reliability: The 1.5L engine and conventional 5-speed automatic are generally durable, and the seller says the car is well maintained and undercoated. At 191k miles, require service records and inspect valve adjustment, plugs and coils, fluids, suspension, wheel bearings, leaks and Northeast rust; undercoating can conceal corrosion.
active.safety: IIHS named the 2012 Fit a Top Safety Pick with Good original moderate-front, side, roof-strength and head-restraint results, but the later driver-side small-overlap test was Poor. Stability control, ABS and side-curtain airbags were standard; its minicar size remains a meaningful disadvantage for a new driver.
active.verdict: New today: an honest-looking, practical hatchback with strong core crash results
active.note: The live individual listing shows a clean title, 191,000 miles, automatic transmission, undercoating, claimed maintenance, a second set of tires and exact-car photos. The VIN and records are not shown, so verify both, check recalls and title history, obtain an insurance quote and require an independent inspection before purchase.
